sources.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, second edition
sources.locator: Chapter 16: printed pp.402–415 (through Theorem 16.17), pp.423–424 (through Theorem 16.32), p.427 Theorem 16.34; pp.428–432 through Exercise 16.44. Printed p = zero-based PDF index minus 17.
sources.read_evidence: Complete parsed PDF passages read using browser, including both local cases and partition cancellation in Theorem 16.11, the finite-parametrization proof, and density coordinate formulas. These are selected ranges, not a claim to have read the corners section or the whole chapter. The negative-chart qualification is explicit on p.405. Fetch-stamp gate is separately recorded in notes.

contents.name: Corollary 16.13
contents.reason: Compact-manifold result included, with noncompact extension requiring compact support of the primitive, not just its derivative.

contents.name: Theorem 16.32 (The Divergence Theorem)
contents.reason: Its proof applies to a supplied positive volume form. Metric-normal formulation is used only in the Euclidean agreement proposition; general Riemannian formulation is deferred below.

contents.name: Proposition 16.38
contents.reason: Use algebraic pullback identities; smoothness is asserted only for local diffeomorphisms. The printed unrestricted smoothness claim (c) fails for x -> x^2 and |dy|.

contents.name: Integration on Lie Groups; Proposition 16.10
contents.reason: Existence and uniqueness of invariant Lie-group integration belongs with Haar measure; no invariant group measure is needed in this partition proof.

contents.name: Exercise 16.31
contents.reason: Orientation independence of Riemannian divergence requires the metric-selected volume density. This page defines divergence relative to a supplied positive volume form.

contents.name: Theorem 16.32: general Riemannian unit-normal formulation
contents.reason: General metric-induced hypersurface volume requires the later Riemannian volume construction. The entire form-theoretic identity is included here, and Euclidean flux is proved here.

sources.title: Will J. Merry, Differential Geometry (2021)
sources.locator: Table of contents PDF p.1; Lecture 26 including Bonus Lecture 26, PDF pp.213–220, numbered results 26.1–26.17; selective Corollaries 27.1–27.2.
sources.read_evidence: Read the full Lecture 26 argument, including 26.8 coordinate independence, 26.12 product-partition proof, 26.14 boundary sign, both steps of 26.16, and the Fubini/FTC cube proof 26.17. The design’s PDF pp.194–207 are not the range in this edition; the actual Lecture 26 starts at PDF p.213.

contents.name: Bonus Lecture 26. Proof of local Stokes
26.3: pairing of singular chains and forms
contents.reason: The chain-form pairing requires singular chain machinery; the current construction integrates top forms directly on oriented manifolds. The later comparison page owns integration over chains.

contents.name: 26.4: pairing descends to homology and cohomology
contents.reason: Descent to homology and de Rham cohomology is the later comparison theorem’s construction, whereas Stokes here is proved without assuming either theory.

contents.name: Corollaries 27.1–27.2: integration and nonzero top cohomology
contents.reason: The nonexact positive top-form consequence is included without cohomology language. The vector-space and pairing formulation is assigned to the de Rham page.

contents.name: Corollaries 27.1–27.2: cohomology formulation
contents.reason: Top de Rham cohomology and integration as a descended functional need the cohomology definitions; the nonexactness mathematical consequence is already included in this batch.

sources.title: Liviu I. Nicolaescu, Lectures on the Geometry of Manifolds, third edition (2020)
sources.locator: Contents p.xiv; §3.4.1 printed pp.111–115; §3.4.2 selected orientation-isomorphism/integration paragraph p.120 through Example 3.4.14 p.121; Examples 3.4.15–3.4.16 pp.121–123. Zero-based PDF index = printed page + 18.
sources.read_evidence: Read §3.4.1 definition, all parts of Example 3.4.2 and Proposition 3.4.3 with its partition proof. Read the signed linear isomorphism from orientation and its gluing formula, the sphere computation, and the Haar/adjoint-trace examples. Not claiming the intervening orientation discussion or §3.4.3 Stokes proof as a second complete Stokes reading.

contents.name: Example 3.4.2(b)
contents.reason: Correct the printed smoothness assertion: |omega| is continuous everywhere and smooth where omega is nonzero; |x||dx| exhibits the failure at zeros.

contents.name: Proposition 3.4.3
contents.reason: Include compact-support smooth-density uniqueness and partition independence using the established Riemann theory. The source uses Lebesgue integration; that extension is only a dependency-free remark here.

contents.name: 3.4.2 Orientability and integration of differential forms: integration paragraph
Definition 3.4.1: general r-densities
contents.reason: Only weight one transforms by the Jacobian needed for the present integration construction. Other weights introduce no prerequisite for Stokes or volume-form divergence.

contents.name: Example 3.4.2(c)
contents.reason: The determinant-of-metric density is a metric-specific construction assigned to the Riemannian volume page. Existence of an arbitrary positive density is proved here without a metric.

contents.name: Example 3.4.15
contents.reason: Bi-invariance of compact-Lie-group Haar integration and averaging representations require the group-invariant development, not the manifold Stokes proof.

contents.name: Example 3.4.16
contents.reason: The adjoint-trace consequence of compact-group invariance uses the Haar construction just deferred; it supplies no missing dependency for form integration.

canonical.name: Computing form integrals by finite parametrizations
canonical.locator: Lee Proposition 16.8 and proof, pp.408–409

support.locator: Lee Proposition 16.8 and proof, pp.408–409
support.support: Let omega be a compactly supported smooth top form on an oriented n-manifold, n>=1.
